title: Separate actionability from visibility in escalations
context: Escalation gating surfaces (CLI exit codes, "needs your call" messages) were counting non-actionable duplicate-id commit-repair followers—entries whose own resolution text says "resolving this requires acting on a different entry first." This inflated decision tallies with entries carrying no direct action. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Introduce Escalation.actionable field (false only for duplicate-id queue followers that are neither drop-target nor apply-target) and actionableEscalations() filter. Gate CLI exit codes and "needs your call" counts on actionable entries only; keep full list in --json/transparency output so nothing is hidden.
consequences: Escalation tallies and user prompts now reflect only decisions the human can actually make directly
Subsequent entry resolution auto-clears dependent non-actionable entries instead of surfacing each as a separate decision
Full queue state remains visible (--json still lists everything) for debugging corrupted repair queues
CLI exits 0 when only non-actionable context remains (avoiding false CI failures)
alternatives_rejected: Omit non-actionable entries entirely—loses transparency about queue state and why certain repairs are queued
Gate on all escalations (original behavior)—conflates context with actionable decisions
Separate escalations into two distinct lists—more complex than single boolean flag on each entry
